## Overview

This notebook asks: does a gene from one of the four significant-LR lists belong to a **real, named, curated KEGG pathway diagram** -- the kind of map you'd recognize (like "Arginine and proline metabolism", but here things like "ECM-receptor interaction" or "PI3K-Akt signaling pathway") -- and if so, does a gene from a *different* cell-type-pair's list also belong to that same diagram? If yes, that's genuine pathway-level convergence between two independently-discovered LR pairs, not just a coincidence of gene names.

**Worked example, checked by hand against KEGG's own database before writing any code here**, using your own Ptn-Sdc4 case plus the Cxcl12-Itgb1 example you raised:

Ptn (the ligand) has **zero** KEGG pathway memberships -- in either the mouse (`mmu:19242`) or human (`hsa:5764`) KEGG gene entry. Pleiotrophin is real, well-studied biology, but it simply isn't part of KEGG's curated pathway network at all. So "Ptn-Sdc4 signaling" can never be placed on a KEGG diagram via the ligand side -- there's nothing to place.

Sdc4 (the receptor) *is* on real maps: ECM-receptor interaction (`mmu04512`), Cell adhesion molecules (`mmu04514`), Cytoskeleton in muscle cells (`mmu04820`), Proteoglycans in cancer (`mmu05205`), and Fluid shear stress and atherosclerosis (`mmu05418`).

Itgb1 (the receptor in your Cxcl12-Itgb1 example) sits on ~26 maps, and four of them are the *same* ones Sdc4 is on: ECM-receptor interaction, Cell adhesion molecules, Cytoskeleton in muscle cells, and Proteoglycans in cancer. Cxcl12 itself (the ligand) is on a completely different set (chemokine/cytokine signaling, NF-kB, axon guidance) that doesn't overlap with Sdc4/Ptn's set at all.

So the convergence you're picturing does happen here -- just at the **receptor** level, not the ligand level: two completely unrelated ligand systems (Ptn and Cxcl12) both drive their respective cell types toward the same handful of canonical ECM/adhesion/proteoglycan pathway maps, via Sdc4 and Itgb1 respectively. That's a real, checkable pattern, and it's exactly the kind of thing this notebook is built to surface systematically across all four of your significant-LR lists rather than one pair at a time by hand.

**Expectation to set going in:** KEGG's curated maps are strongest for classical metabolic and well-established signaling pathways (chemokines, integrins, ECM receptors, GPCR cascades); more specialized developmental growth-factor systems (Ptn/Ptprz1/midkine family, and likely others in your lists) are comparatively under-annotated -- Ptn's zero hits being the clearest example. Don't expect every gene, or even every pair, to land on a map. Receptors tend to be more "generic" molecules and show up far more often than specialized ligands do, so most of the convergence signal will likely show up receptor-side or via broad hub pathways (ECM-receptor interaction, Focal adhesion, PI3K-Akt signaling), not pair-specific ones.

```{r setup}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)

if (!requireNamespace("KEGGREST", quietly = TRUE)) {
  if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("BiocManager")
  BiocManager::install("KEGGREST", update = FALSE, ask = FALSE)
}
library(KEGGREST)
```

## Helpers: exact-match KEGG gene resolution + pathway membership, with local caching

`KEGGREST::keggFind()` does a **substring** search across gene names and aliases -- searching "Ptn" also returns `Ptpn4`, `Xcl1`, `Optn`, `Rptn`, `Alpl`, `Kptn`, `Nptn`, etc. The resolver below filters those hits down to an exact (case-insensitive) match against the gene's own alias list, so it doesn't silently pick the wrong gene.

Results are cached to a local RDS file, since KEGG's REST API is free for academic/personal use but rate-limited and shouldn't be hammered on every re-render.

```{r kegg-helpers}
#| label: kegg-helpers

kegg_cache_path <- "kegg_pathway_cache.rds"
kegg_cache <- if (file.exists(kegg_cache_path)) readRDS(kegg_cache_path) else list()

save_kegg_cache <- function() saveRDS(kegg_cache, kegg_cache_path)

#' Resolve a gene symbol to its exact KEGG gene ID (e.g. "mmu:19242") for a
#' given organism code ("mmu" = mouse, "hsa" = human). Returns NA if no exact
#' match is found among that gene's own alias list.
resolve_kegg_gene_id <- function(gene_symbol, organism = "mmu") {
  hits <- tryCatch(KEGGREST::keggFind(organism, gene_symbol), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(hits) || length(hits) == 0) return(NA_character_)

  # hits is a named character vector: names = "mmu:19242", values = "Ptn, HARP, ...; pleiotrophin precursor"
  aliases_by_hit <- hits %>%
    stringr::str_split(";") %>%
    purrr::map_chr(1) %>%                     # keep only the alias list, drop the description after ";"
    stringr::str_split(",\\s*")

  exact_match <- purrr::map_lgl(aliases_by_hit, ~ gene_symbol %in% .x)
  matched_ids <- names(hits)[exact_match]

  if (length(matched_ids) == 0) return(NA_character_)
  matched_ids[1]  # first exact match if somehow more than one
}

#' Full mouse pathway id -> name lookup table, fetched once and cached
#' (one API call returns all ~560 mouse pathways; joining against this
#' locally is far more robust than querying KEGG per-pathway-id -- KEGG's
#' /list endpoint 404s on a specific "path:mmuXXXXX" entry, confirmed by
#' testing directly against the live API before relying on it here).
get_mmu_pathway_names <- function() {
  cache_key <- "mmu_pathway_names_table"
  if (!is.null(kegg_cache[[cache_key]])) return(kegg_cache[[cache_key]])

  raw <- KEGGREST::keggList("pathway", "mmu")
  tbl <- tibble(pathway_id = names(raw), pathway_name = stringr::str_remove(unname(raw), " - .*$"))

  kegg_cache[[cache_key]] <<- tbl
  save_kegg_cache()
  tbl
}
mmu_pathway_names <- get_mmu_pathway_names()

#' Get the set of KEGG pathway IDs + names a gene belongs to. Cached.
get_kegg_pathways <- function(gene_symbol, organism = "mmu") {
  cache_key <- paste(organism, gene_symbol, sep = "::")
  if (!is.null(kegg_cache[[cache_key]])) return(kegg_cache[[cache_key]])

  kegg_id <- resolve_kegg_gene_id(gene_symbol, organism)
  result <- if (is.na(kegg_id)) {
    tibble(gene = gene_symbol, kegg_id = NA_character_, pathway_id = NA_character_, pathway_name = NA_character_)
  } else {
    links <- tryCatch(KEGGREST::keggLink("pathway", kegg_id), error = function(e) character(0))
    if (length(links) == 0) {
      tibble(gene = gene_symbol, kegg_id = kegg_id, pathway_id = NA_character_, pathway_name = NA_character_)
    } else {
      pathway_ids <- stringr::str_remove(unname(links), "^path:")
      tibble(gene = gene_symbol, kegg_id = kegg_id, pathway_id = pathway_ids) %>%
        dplyr::left_join(mmu_pathway_names, by = "pathway_id")
    }
  }

  kegg_cache[[cache_key]] <<- result
  save_kegg_cache()
  Sys.sleep(0.34)  # be polite to the free KEGG REST API (~3 req/sec)
  result
}
```

## Load the four significant-LR lists

Earlier drafts of this notebook read every raw `ligand_complex`/`receptor_complex` value straight out of the full `liana_*_by_age.csv` files -- i.e. every candidate pair LIANA+ tested, not just the ones that actually held up. This version instead reads `significant_lr_pairs.csv`, exported by `03_RCTD_SpotDeconvolution.qmd`'s "Export the curated (3-metric-agreement) significant LR pairs" section: exactly the pairs where spatial slope, spatial detection enrichment, and scRNA `magnitude_rank` all agree in sign on their young-to-old shift (`compare_spatial_to_liana()`'s `agreement_check`) -- the same pairs shown in the `plot_cross_modality_trajectory()` plots. If you haven't re-rendered `03_RCTD_SpotDeconvolution.qmd`'s export chunk since it was added, run that chunk once first so `significant_lr_pairs.csv` exists alongside the `liana_*_by_age.csv` files.

```{r load-lr-lists}
#| label: load-lr-lists

# Named only for display / for the pathview color-coding step further down --
# no longer used to pick which file to read.
spatial_pair_labels <- c("Astrocyte-Vascular", "Vascular-Microglia",
                          "OPC-Cajal-Retzius", "Neurogenic_lineage-GC")

sig_pairs <- readr::read_csv("significant_lr_pairs.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  distinct(spatial_pair, ligand_complex, receptor_complex)

# Complexes come through as e.g. "GeneA_GeneB" -- split those into individual
# subunits before KEGG lookup, since KEGG genes are single proteins.
split_complex <- function(x) stringr::str_split(x, "_")

lr_gene_sets <- purrr::pmap(sig_pairs, function(spatial_pair, ligand_complex, receptor_complex) {
  ligands   <- unlist(split_complex(ligand_complex))
  receptors <- unlist(split_complex(receptor_complex))
  tibble(
    spatial_pair = spatial_pair,
    gene = unique(c(ligands, receptors)),
    role = ifelse(unique(c(ligands, receptors)) %in% ligands, "ligand", "receptor")
    # note: a gene acting as both ligand and receptor across different rows
    # will just get whichever role its first occurrence had -- role is
    # informational only and doesn't affect the pathway lookup below.
  )
})

lr_genes_long <- bind_rows(lr_gene_sets) %>% distinct(spatial_pair, gene, role)
lr_genes_long
```

## Cross-reference every gene against KEGG pathway membership

This is the step that hits the KEGG API (cached after the first run, so re-rendering is fast).

```{r kegg-crossref}
#| label: kegg-crossref

unique_genes <- unique(lr_genes_long$gene)

gene_pathway_map <- purrr::map_dfr(unique_genes, get_kegg_pathways) %>%
  filter(!is.na(pathway_id))

# Join back to spatial_pair (a gene can appear in more than one LR list) --
# keep role here (not just spatial_pair/gene) since convergence-detail below
# selects it back out.
gene_pathway_by_pair <- lr_genes_long %>%
  distinct(spatial_pair, gene, role) %>%
  inner_join(gene_pathway_map, by = "gene")

gene_pathway_by_pair
```

## Convergence pathways: hit by 2+ different cell-type-pair analyses

```{r convergence}
#| label: convergence

convergence_pathways <- gene_pathway_by_pair %>%
  distinct(spatial_pair, pathway_id, pathway_name, gene) %>%
  group_by(pathway_id, pathway_name) %>%
  summarise(
    n_spatial_pairs_hitting_it = n_distinct(spatial_pair),
    n_distinct_genes           = n_distinct(gene),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n_spatial_pairs_hitting_it >= 2) %>%
  # The interesting case is *different* genes from different lists landing on
  # the same pathway (e.g. Sdc4 from one list, Itgb1 from another) -- that's
  # real pathway-level convergence between independently-discovered pairs.
  # n_distinct_genes == 1 means it's the same single gene just reused across
  # lists (e.g. one shared receptor), which is a narrower, less interesting
  # kind of "hit" worth sorting separately rather than mixing in at the top.
  arrange(desc(n_distinct_genes > 1), desc(n_spatial_pairs_hitting_it))

convergence_pathways
```

For each convergence pathway, which genes (and from which spatial pair) actually land there:

```{r convergence-detail}
#| label: convergence-detail

convergence_detail <- gene_pathway_by_pair %>%
  semi_join(convergence_pathways, by = "pathway_id") %>%
  arrange(pathway_id, spatial_pair) %>%
  dplyr::select(pathway_id, pathway_name, spatial_pair, gene, role)

convergence_detail
```

write_csv(convergence_pathways, "kegg_convergence_pathways.csv")

## Sanity check against the hand-verified Ptn/Sdc4 vs Cxcl12/Itgb1 result

Confirms the pipeline reproduces the manually-checked result from the overview above (assuming Cxcl12/Itgb1 are actually present somewhere in your significant lists -- adjust if not):

```{r sanity-check}
#| label: sanity-check

gene_pathway_by_pair %>%
  filter(gene %in% c("Ptn", "Sdc4", "Cxcl12", "Itgb1")) %>%
  dplyr::select(gene, pathway_id, pathway_name, spatial_pair) %>%
  arrange(gene, pathway_id)
```

## Notes on interpretation

A pathway showing up as "convergent" here means genes from two different cell-type-pair analyses both belong to that named KEGG map -- it does not mean the two LR pairs interact directly, only that both push their respective cell types toward the same broader curated pathway territory (e.g., both toward ECM/adhesion signaling, or both toward PI3K-Akt signaling). Treat it as a hypothesis about shared downstream biology worth a closer look, not a proven mechanistic link. `07_STRING_NetworkAnalysis.qmd` asks the same convergence question from a different angle -- functional-association network structure and data-driven clustering rather than curated numbered-pathway membership -- and is a good cross-check once you've identified an interesting convergence pathway here.

Zero KEGG hits for a gene (like Ptn) is a coverage gap in KEGG's curated network, not evidence the gene lacks real signaling function -- it just means that particular ligand family isn't well represented in KEGG's pathway diagrams. A gene with no hits simply won't appear in `gene_pathway_map` at all; it's still a real, significant LR pair, it just can't be placed on a KEGG-style picture this way.

Complex ligands/receptors (e.g. multi-subunit entries with an underscore) are split into individual subunits before lookup -- a convergence hit driven by one subunit of a complex is still worth noting, but keep in mind the complex may function as a unit even if only one subunit happens to be KEGG-annotated.

A `n_distinct_genes == 1` convergence row (in the `convergence_pathways` table above) means the *same* gene was simply reused across two of your significant-LR lists (e.g. one shared receptor) -- that's a narrower finding than two genuinely *different* genes from two lists landing on the same pathway map, which is the Ptn-Sdc4/Cxcl12-Itgb1-style convergence this notebook was built to surface. Rows are sorted so multi-gene hits come first; single-gene reuse hits are still shown, just lower priority.

Gene symbol drift is a real, recurring issue worth expecting, not a one-off: KEGG's own alias resolution and Bioconductor's `org.Mm.eg.db` don't always agree on which symbol is "current" for a gene that MGI has renamed (e.g. `Atp5b` -> `Atp5f1b`). The pathview-rendering step below falls back from `SYMBOL` to `ALIAS` lookup to handle this, and prints a message naming any gene it still can't resolve either way -- if that happens, the gene is real, it's just that neither keytype in the currently-installed `org.Mm.eg.db` recognizes the exact string coming out of KEGG's alias list.

## Optional: render the actual KEGG diagram with your genes highlighted

This reproduces the picture-style output (the same visual family as the reference map you attached) using `pathview`, coloring each gene by which of your four cell-type-pair lists it came from. Heavier dependency chain than the rest of this notebook (needs `org.Mm.eg.db` for symbol-to-Entrez mapping, ~200+MB), so it's kept separate and off by default -- install and flip `eval: true` below once you've identified a convergence pathway above that you want to actually see.

```{r pathview-setup}
#| label: pathview-setup
#| eval: false

if (!requireNamespace("pathview", quietly = TRUE)) BiocManager::install("pathview", update = FALSE, ask = FALSE)
if (!requireNamespace("org.Mm.eg.db", quietly = TRUE)) BiocManager::install("org.Mm.eg.db", update = FALSE, ask = FALSE)
library(pathview)     # must be attached via library(), not just requireNamespace()/pathview:: --
                       # pathview's own internal data(bods) call (a known upstream bug: unlike
                       # its sibling call for "korg", it omits package="pathview") can only find
                       # bods when the package is actually on the search path.
library(org.Mm.eg.db) # also needs to be genuinely attached, not just installed -- pathview's
                       # own internal SYMBOL->Entrez mapping silently fails ("None of the keys
                       # entered are valid keys for 'SYMBOL'") when it can't resolve this, which
                       # is why the render chunk below does the mapping explicitly itself instead
                       # of relying on pathview's gene.idtype = "SYMBOL" auto-detection.

# Known pathview bug workaround ("object 'bods' not found", reported repeatedly on
# Bioconductor support and in downstream packages like pathfindR): force-load the
# dataset explicitly before ever calling pathview(). If THIS line itself errors with
# "data set 'bods' not found", that means the local pathview install is missing its
# data files (a broken/incomplete install, not a scoping issue) -- the fix there is
# BiocManager::install("pathview", force = TRUE) to reinstall it cleanly.
data(bods, package = "pathview")
data(korg, package = "pathview")

# If pathview() below still throws the same error even after the above (rare, but
# reported to happen with some pathview/Bioconductor version combinations), the
# community-documented fallback is to fully detach and reattach it once in the
# session, which forces a clean re-registration of its lazy-loaded data:
#   detach("package:pathview", unload = TRUE); library(pathview)
```

```{r pathview-render}
#| label: pathview-render
#| eval: false

# Example: render the top convergence pathway from the table above.
target_pathway_id <- stringr::str_remove(convergence_pathways$pathway_id[1], "^mmu")

# Encode which spatial_pair(s) hit each gene as a simple numeric code (a gene
# hit by only one list gets that list's code; a gene hit by multiple lists
# gets flagged distinctly). This is a categorical label repurposed as
# pathview's expected numeric "gene.data" -- colors are group labels here,
# not magnitudes.
pair_codes <- setNames(seq_along(spatial_pair_labels), spatial_pair_labels)

gene_group_code <- gene_pathway_by_pair %>%
  filter(pathway_id == convergence_pathways$pathway_id[1]) %>%
  distinct(gene, spatial_pair) %>%
  group_by(gene) %>%
  summarise(code = if (n() > 1) length(spatial_pair_labels) + 1 else pair_codes[spatial_pair[1]], .groups = "drop")

gene_data_vec <- setNames(gene_group_code$code, gene_group_code$gene)

# Root cause of the earlier "None of the keys entered are valid keys for
# 'SYMBOL'" error, confirmed by inspection: it wasn't a species/attach issue
# at all -- it was one specific stale gene symbol. MGI renamed the ATP
# synthase subunit genes some years back (Atp5b -> Atp5f1b, etc.); KEGG's own
# alias list still recognizes the old name "Atp5b" (that's how it resolved
# earlier in this notebook's KEGGREST lookups), but org.Mm.eg.db's current
# SYMBOL keytype only accepts the new name -- "Atp5b" now lives under ALIAS,
# not SYMBOL. AnnotationDbi::mapIds() hard-errors (rather than returning NA)
# when *zero* of the supplied keys match at all, which is exactly what
# happened with a single-gene pathway where that one gene was the stale name.
#
# Fix: try SYMBOL first, then fall back to ALIAS for anything unresolved,
# with each attempt wrapped so a total mismatch degrades to "nothing
# resolved" instead of aborting the whole render.
map_symbol_to_entrez <- function(gene_symbols, orgdb = org.Mm.eg.db) {
  safe_map <- function(keys_vec, keytype) {
    if (length(keys_vec) == 0) return(character(0))
    tryCatch(
      AnnotationDbi::mapIds(orgdb, keys = keys_vec, column = "ENTREZID", keytype = keytype, multiVals = "first"),
      error = function(e) setNames(rep(NA_character_, length(keys_vec)), keys_vec)
    )
  }

  primary <- safe_map(gene_symbols, "SYMBOL")
  unresolved <- names(primary)[is.na(primary)]
  if (length(unresolved) > 0) {
    # ALIAS can be ambiguous (one legacy name occasionally maps to more than
    # one current gene) -- multiVals = "first" just takes one, fine for this
    # exploratory rendering.
    fallback <- safe_map(unresolved, "ALIAS")
    still_na <- is.na(fallback)
    primary[names(fallback)[!still_na]] <- fallback[!still_na]
  }
  primary
}

entrez_ids <- map_symbol_to_entrez(names(gene_data_vec))

gene_data_entrez <- gene_data_vec
names(gene_data_entrez) <- unname(entrez_ids[names(gene_data_vec)])
unmapped <- gene_group_code$gene[is.na(names(gene_data_entrez))]
if (length(unmapped) > 0) {
  message("Dropping gene(s) with no org.Mm.eg.db Entrez match (via SYMBOL or ALIAS): ", paste(unmapped, collapse = ", "))
}
gene_data_entrez <- gene_data_entrez[!is.na(names(gene_data_entrez))]

if (length(gene_data_entrez) == 0) {
  stop("None of this pathway's genes resolved to an Entrez ID via org.Mm.eg.db -- ",
       "check gene symbol spelling/casing in the significant-LR CSVs.")
}

# Calling the bare, attached function here (not pathview::pathview()) --
# see the note in pathview-setup above about why that matters for its
# internal data(bods) lookup.
pathview(
  gene.data   = gene_data_entrez,
  pathway.id  = target_pathway_id,
  species     = "mmu",
  gene.idtype = "entrez",  # pathview's default; explicit here since we're now passing real Entrez IDs
  out.suffix  = "convergence",
  kegg.native = TRUE
)
# Produces mmu<target_pathway_id>.convergence.png in the working directory --
# the official KEGG diagram with your genes colored by contributing list.
```
